title: AI for Software Design: Behavioral Programming
shortDescription: Model independent software requirements as b-threads, coordinate them through Request-Wait-Block synchronization, and verify a safety invariant.
learningOutcomes: Model software requirements as independent behavioral threads.
Apply Request-Wait-Block synchronization to coordinate concurrent requirements.
Implement a safety invariant without modifying the functional behavior threads.
Verify behavioral traces using executable assertions rather than structural checks alone.
Critically evaluate modularity, coupling, determinism, and deadlock in requirement-oriented software design.

tasks.title: Understand the behavioral coordinator
tasks.description: Trace how BProgram collects requests and blocks, selects events, and resumes interested b-threads.

tasks.title: Complete functional behavior
tasks.description: Implement the cold-water b-thread from the supplied hot-water example.

tasks.title: Implement the safety invariant
tasks.description: Create an independent overflow-prevention b-thread that blocks fill events and requests draining at capacity.

tasks.title: Model and verify the design
tasks.description: Complete the visual architecture and pass semantic public tests over the execution trace.

tasks.title: Analyse and report
tasks.description: Stress-test configuration changes and document evidence and critical analysis in the integrated report.
